sources.citation: Syarfina, Tengku, Alika Sandra Hasibuan & Lusiana Sinaga. 2023. Stress in Angkola Batak Language: An Acoustic Phonetic Approach. LINGTERSA (Linguistik, Terjemahan, Sastra) 4(2): 46-53. DOI 10.32734/lingtersa.v4i2.13451 (open, CC BY-SA).

sources.quote: Claims word-INITIAL stress in Angkola, from F0/intensity/duration of words inside 5 declarative sentences, 5 speakers (Padangsidimpuan Hutaimbaru), Praat. Formally contradicts van der Tuuk's final/penult window, but the evidence is weak: 'stress' = highest F0 per word in running declaratives (declination confound, sentence-initial verbs), one token per word, no minimal pairs, and the discussion itself says (p.52) 'word stress is in the position of the penultimate syllable' before concluding 'first syllable'; for all disyllables initial = penult anyway. Should be noted in the record as a dissen
sources.locator: Abstract p.46; Results p.50-51 (Tables 1-2); Conclusion p.52: 'the position of declarative sentence stress in the Angkola Batak language is located at the beginning of the word or first syllable' (mangan -> má-, utte -> út-, mamasu -> má-, sikola -> sí-, mardahan -> már-).

sources.citation: Adelaar, K. A. 1981. Reconstruction of Proto-Batak phonology. NUSA: Linguistic Studies in Indonesian and Languages in Indonesia 10: 1-20. Jakarta: Badan Penyelenggara Seri NUSA.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Southern Batak (Toba, Angkola, Mandailing) has distinctive (lexical/syntactically conditioned) accent on penult or ultima (Toba minimal pairs /sogot/, /tanom/~/tanóm/, /bau/~/baú/); polymorphemic words penult except excessive/comparative suffixes and affixed monosyllabic stems. Adelaar's An/Ma data are drawn from van der Tuuk and Eggink 1936, so this is a 1981 comparative restatement, not new fieldwork on Angkola stress.
sources.locator: sec. 4 (Mandailing) p.8: 'The Mandailing phoneme system differs from the Toba system only in minor details'; sec. 5 (Angkola) p.8-9: differs from Mandailing only in listed segmental respects, no separate accent section; sec. 3.4 (Toba accent) p.5; Part II sec. 10 p.16: 'In the southern dialects [To, An, Ma] and in Simalungun the accent is distinctive and its position is syntactically determined (see par. 3.4 and 6.3). Polymorphemic words have the accent on the penultima, irrespective of their syntactical position (except in cases treated in par. 3.4.2 and 6.4.3). In the Northern dialects accent is not distinctive'; also item (f) p.14 'distinctive accent is a common innovation in SB and Si'.
